Proposed short-term actions (will update MAP_v3.xlsx and attach):
- Freeze feature/parameter changes on the production cutover pipeline until acceptance closes (owner: Rishi).
- Open a focused QA window for Helix to validate security fixes; Redwood will provide a priority support queue and a pre-warmed KV cache snapshot for the first 48h of acceptance (owner: Jonas).
- If acceptance stretches beyond the one-week rebaseline, we will provide a staged rollback and a one-time account credit discussion (owner: Marissa / Sales Ops).

Can Helix procurement confirm which of the security questions are gating vs informational so we can prioritize engineering work?

I'm scheduling an internal alignment at 11:00 PT to lock owners and update the MAP. If that works for you, we will circulate a refreshed timeline and risk log entry by EOD.

Neha / team — quick technical readout on containment options: 
- We can enable a dedicated priority pool on Redwood Dedicated for Helix traffic for the first 72 hours post-cutover; this requires a config change but no infra lead time. That reduces risk of throttling during extended QA.
- KV cache warmup: Jonas' team can seed prefix caches for the acceptance test users to avoid cold-start token spends.
- If Helix needs an extended rollback window (>2 weeks), we should evaluate a limited read-only mode to contain business risk without full rollback.

Impact on billing/credits: engineering containment is low-cost; any compensation conversations should go via Sales Ops (Marissa) — we can provide telemetry proving containment worked if needed.

I'll join the 11:00 alignment and will bring a quick runbook for priority routing and cache warmup.
